title.en: Volume 68 Biographies 33: Yu Wenkai, Yan Pi, He Chou
title.raw: 卷68 列傳第33 宇文愷 閻毗 何稠 Volume 68 Biographies 33: Yu Wenkai, Yan Pi, He Chou

sentences.zh: 宇文愷，字安樂，杞國公忻之弟也。

translations.literal: Yu Wenkai, Yu Wenkai, courtesy name Anle, was the younger brother of Duke of Qi Xin.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Wenkai, whose courtesy name was Anle, was the younger brother of the Duke of Qi, Xin.

sentences.zh: 在周，以功臣子，年三歲，賜爵雙泉伯，七歲，進封安平郡公，邑二千戶。

translations.literal: Under the Zhou, as the son of a meritorious minister, at age three he was granted the title Baron of Shuangquan; at age seven he was advanced to Duke of Anping Commandery, with a fief of two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: During the Northern Zhou, as the son of a meritorious minister, he received the title Baron of Shuangquan at age three and was promoted to Duke of Anping Commandery at age seven, with a fief of two thousand households.

sentences.zh: 愷少有器局。

translations.literal: Kai from youth had capacity and breadth of mind.
translations.idiomatic: From an early age, Yu Wenkai showed great talent and breadth of vision.

sentences.zh: 家世武將，諸兄並以弓馬自達，愷獨好學，博覽書記，解屬文，多伎藝，號為名父公子。

translations.literal: His family for generations were military generals; all his elder brothers achieved advancement through bow and horse, but Kai alone loved learning, broadly read books and records, understood literary composition, and had many skills and arts, and was called a son of a famous father.
translations.idiomatic: His family had long been a line of military men, and all his elder brothers made their way through archery and horsemanship. Yu Wenkai alone loved learning, read widely in books and records, was skilled at literary composition, and mastered many crafts. He was known as a son worthy of his distinguished father.

sentences.zh: 初為千牛，累遷禦正中大夫、儀同三司。

translations.literal: At first he served as Thousand-Ox [guard], and was repeatedly promoted to Supervising Director of the Imperial Clan and Yitong Third Rank.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a Thousand-Ox guard and rose through successive appointments to Supervising Director of the Imperial Clan and Yitong Third Rank.

sentences.zh: 高祖為丞相，加上開府中大夫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen was Chancellor, he was additionally appointed Supervising Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen was still Chancellor, Yu Wenkai was further appointed Supervising Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 及踐阼，誅宇文氏，愷初亦在殺中，以其與周本別，兄忻有功于國，使人馳赦之，僅而得免。

translations.literal: When he ascended the throne, the Yuwen clan was executed; Kai at first was also among those to be killed, but because his branch was separate from the Zhou royal house and his elder brother Xin had rendered service to the state, the emperor sent a messenger racing to pardon him, and he barely escaped.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen took the throne, he executed the Yuwen clan. Yu Wenkai was initially marked for death as well, but because his branch of the family was distinct from the Zhou royal house and his elder brother Xin had served the state with merit, the emperor sent a messenger posthaste to pardon him, and he barely escaped with his life.

sentences.zh: 後拜營宗廟副監、太子左庶子。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Deputy Supervisor of the Construction of the Ancestral Temple and Left Assistant to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed Deputy Supervisor of the Construction of the Ancestral Temple and Left Assistant to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 廟成，別封甑山縣公，邑千戶。

translations.literal: When the temple was completed, he was separately enfeoffed as Duke of Zengshan County, with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: When the temple was completed, he received a separate enfeoffment as Duke of Zengshan County, with a fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 及遷都，上以愷有巧思，詔領營新都副監。

translations.literal: When the capital was moved, the emperor, because Kai had ingenious ideas, ordered him to take charge as Deputy Supervisor of the Construction of the New Capital.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital was relocated, the emperor, recognizing Yu Wenkai's ingenious mind, appointed him Deputy Supervisor of the Construction of the New Capital.

sentences.zh: 高熲雖總大綱，凡所規畫，皆出於愷。

translations.literal: Although Gao Jiong held overall authority, all planning and design came from Kai.
translations.idiomatic: Although Gao Jiong held overall authority, every plan and design came from Yu Wenkai.

sentences.zh: 後決渭水達河，以通運漕，詔愷總督其事。

translations.literal: Later the Wei River was cut through to reach the Yellow River to open transport and grain shipment; the emperor ordered Kai to supervise the whole affair.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the Wei River was cut through to the Yellow River to open a transport canal, the emperor put Yu Wenkai in overall charge of the project.

sentences.zh: 後拜萊州刺史，甚有能名。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Governor of Laizhou and gained a great reputation for ability.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed Governor of Laizhou, where he earned a strong reputation for competence.

sentences.zh: 兄忻被誅，除名於家，久不得調。

translations.literal: When his elder brother Xin was executed, he was struck from the family register and for a long time could not be reassigned.
translations.idiomatic: After his elder brother Xin was executed, Yu Wenkai was struck from the family register and went for a long time without a new appointment.

sentences.zh: 會朝廷以魯班故道久絕不行，令愷修復之。

translations.literal: It happened that the court, because the old Lu Ban route had long been abandoned and impassable, ordered Kai to restore it.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the court found that the old Lu Ban canal route had long been abandoned and impassable, and ordered Yu Wenkai to restore it.

sentences.zh: 既而上建仁壽宮，訪可任者，右僕射楊素言愷有巧思，上然之，於是檢校將作大匠。

translations.literal: Soon afterward the emperor built Renshou Palace and sought someone fit for the task; Right Vice Director Yang Su said Kai had ingenious ideas, and the emperor agreed; thereupon he was appointed Acting Chief of Palace Construction.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the emperor began building Renshou Palace and sought someone capable of overseeing it. Right Vice Director Yang Su recommended Yu Wenkai for his ingenious mind, and the emperor agreed, appointing him Acting Chief of Palace Construction.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，拜仁壽宮監，授儀同三司，尋為將作少監。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was appointed Supervisor of Renshou Palace, granted Yitong Third Rank, and soon became Deputy Chief of Palace Construction.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he was made Supervisor of Renshou Palace and granted Yitong Third Rank, and soon afterward became Deputy Chief of Palace Construction.

sentences.zh: 文獻皇后崩，愷與楊素營山陵事，上善之，複爵安平郡公，邑千戶。

translations.literal: When Empress Wenxian died, Kai together with Yang Su undertook the construction of the imperial tomb; the emperor approved of this and restored his title as Duke of Anping Commandery, with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wenxian died, Yu Wenkai and Yang Su oversaw the construction of her tomb. The emperor was pleased and restored his title as Duke of Anping Commandery, with a fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 煬帝即位，遷都洛陽，以愷為營東都副監，尋遷將作大匠。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne and moved the capital to Luoyang, Kai was appointed Deputy Supervisor of the Construction of the Eastern Capital, and soon was promoted to Chief of Palace Construction.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang took the throne and moved the capital to Luoyang, Yu Wenkai was appointed Deputy Supervisor of the Construction of the Eastern Capital and soon promoted to Chief of Palace Construction.

sentences.zh: 愷揣帝心在宏侈，於是東京制度窮極壯麗。

translations.literal: Kai surmised that the emperor's heart lay in grandeur and extravagance, and so the institutions of the Eastern Capital were pushed to the utmost in magnificence.
translations.idiomatic: Reading the emperor's taste for grandeur and extravagance, Yu Wenkai designed the Eastern Capital to the utmost in scale and splendor.

sentences.zh: 帝大悅之，進位開府，拜工部尚書。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased, promoted him to the rank of Kaifu, and appointed him Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased, promoted him to Kaifu rank, and appointed him Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 及長城之役，詔愷規度之。

translations.literal: When the Great Wall project was undertaken, the emperor ordered Kai to plan and measure it.
translations.idiomatic: When work on the Great Wall began, the emperor ordered Yu Wenkai to plan and survey it.

sentences.zh: 時帝北巡，欲誇戎狄，令愷為大帳，其下坐數千人。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor toured the north and wished to impress the barbarians; he ordered Kai to make a great tent under which several thousand people could sit.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor toured the north and wished to impress the frontier peoples, he had Yu Wenkai build a great tent large enough to seat several thousand people beneath it.

sentences.zh: 帝大悅，賜物千段。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and bestowed one thousand bolts of goods.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted and rewarded him with one thousand bolts of goods.

sentences.zh: 又造觀風行殿，上容侍衛者數百人，離合為之，下施輪軸，推移倏忽，有若神功。

translations.literal: He also built the Wind-Viewing Mobile Hall, which could hold several hundred attendants and guards on its upper level; it was made in sections that could be joined and separated, with wheels and axles beneath, so that it could be moved in an instant, as if by divine power.
translations.idiomatic: He also built the Wind-Viewing Mobile Hall, whose upper level could hold several hundred attendants and guards. Assembled in detachable sections and mounted on wheels and axles below, it could be moved in an instant, as if by supernatural craft.

sentences.zh: 戎狄見之，莫不驚駭。

translations.literal: When the barbarians saw it, none failed to be astonished and awed.
translations.idiomatic: The frontier peoples who saw it were all struck with astonishment.

sentences.zh: 帝彌悅焉，前後賞賚，不可勝紀。

translations.literal: The emperor was all the more pleased; rewards before and after were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was still more pleased, and the rewards he received before and after were beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 自永嘉之亂，明堂廢絕，隋有天下，將復古制，議者紛然，皆不能決。

translations.literal: Since the chaos of the Yongjia era, the Bright Hall had been abandoned and cut off; when the Sui possessed the realm, they wished to restore the ancient institution, but debaters were divided and none could decide.
translations.idiomatic: Since the chaos of the Yongjia era, the Bright Hall had fallen into disuse. When the Sui gained the realm and sought to restore the ancient institution, debate raged on all sides, and no decision could be reached.

sentences.zh: 愷博考群籍，奏《明堂議表》曰：

translations.literal: Kai broadly examined the various texts and submitted a "Memorial on the Bright Hall Debate," saying:
translations.idiomatic: Yu Wenkai examined the various texts at length and submitted a "Memorial on the Bright Hall Debate," which read:

sentences.zh: 臣聞在天成象，房心為布政之宮，在地成形，丙午居正陽之位。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that in Heaven forms are completed, and Fang and Xin are the palace of dispensing government; on Earth forms take shape, and Bing-Wu occupies the position of true yang.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject has heard that Heaven completes its signs, with the stars Fang and Xin forming the palace of governance, and that Earth takes shape below, with the Bing-Wu position occupying the seat of true yang.

sentences.zh: 觀雲告月，順生殺之序；

translations.literal: Observing clouds and announcing the moon follow the sequence of generation and killing;
translations.idiomatic: Reading the clouds and proclaiming the seasons follows the order of growth and decline;

sentences.zh: 五室九宮，統人神之際。

translations.literal: the five chambers and nine palaces unite the realm between men and spirits.
translations.idiomatic: the five chambers and nine palaces unite the realms of men and spirits.

sentences.zh: 金口木舌，發令兆民；

translations.literal: The golden mouth and wooden tongue issue commands to the myriad people;
translations.idiomatic: Through the bell and clapper, commands go forth to the myriad people;

sentences.zh: 玉瓚黃琮，式嚴宗祀。

translations.literal: the jade libation cup and yellow jade square perform solemn ancestral sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: with jade libation vessels and yellow jade squares to solemnize ancestral rites.

sentences.zh: 何嘗不矜莊扆寧，盡妙思於規摹，凝睟冕旒，致子來於矩矱。

translations.literal: When had they not been dignified and solemn at the imperial screen, exhausting ingenious thought in planning and design, gazing intently beneath the imperial crown, and drawing people to come of their own accord to the measuring square?
translations.idiomatic: Never were they less than dignified and solemn beneath the imperial screen, exhausting every refinement of design, gazing with fixed attention beneath the crown, and drawing the people to come of their own accord to the measured plan.

sentences.zh: 伏惟皇帝陛下，提衡握契，禦辯乘乾，減五登三，複上皇之化，流凶去暴，丕下武之緒。

translations.literal: Your subject humbly considers that Your Majesty, holding the balance and grasping the tally, riding the argument and mounting Qian, reducing five and ascending three, has restored the transformation of the Supreme Emperor, flowing away the vicious and removing the violent, and greatly continuing the line of King Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject humbly considers that Your Majesty, holding the scales of justice and grasping the mandate, mounted on the throne in accordance with Heaven, has reduced the Five Emperors and ascended to the Three Sovereigns, restoring the governance of the Supreme Emperor, sweeping away the wicked and the violent, and greatly continuing the legacy of King Wu.

sentences.zh: 用百姓之異心，驅一代以同域，康哉康哉，民無能而名矣。

translations.literal: Using the differing hearts of the common people, he drove one generation into one realm; how prosperous, how prosperous — the people have no words with which to name it.
translations.idiomatic: He has harmonized the differing hearts of the people and united the age in one realm. How prosperous, how prosperous — the people have no words adequate to praise it.

sentences.zh: 故使天符地寶，吐醴飛甘，造物資生，澄源反樸。

translations.literal: Therefore Heaven's signs and Earth's treasures appear, sweet dew rises and sweetness flies, the Creator nourishes life, and the source is clarified and simplicity restored.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's signs and Earth's treasures have appeared, sweet dew rises and blessings descend, the Creator nourishes all life, and the source is clarified and simplicity restored.

sentences.zh: 九圍清謐，四表削平，襲我衣冠，齊其文軌。

translations.literal: The nine domains are clear and tranquil, the four quarters are cut level, they inherit our robes and caps, and align their script and tracks.
translations.idiomatic: The nine domains are peaceful and still, the four quarters are pacified, foreign peoples adopt our robes and caps, and align their writing and their roads with ours.

sentences.zh: 茫茫上玄，陳珪璧之敬；

translations.literal: To the vast Supreme Mystery, he presents the reverence of jade disks and jade rings;
translations.idiomatic: Before the vast Supreme Mystery, he presents the reverence due to jade disks and rings;

sentences.zh: 肅肅清廟，感霜露之誠。

translations.literal: in the solemn and pure temple, he feels the sincerity of frost and dew.
translations.idiomatic: in the solemn ancestral temple, he feels the sincerity owed to frost and dew.

sentences.zh: 正金奏《九韶》、《六莖》之樂，定石渠五官、三雍之禮。

translations.literal: He rectifies the golden performance of the music "Nine Shao" and "Six Stalks," and fixes the ritual of the Stone Channel's Five Offices and Three Yong.
translations.idiomatic: He has set right the golden performance of the Nine Shao and Six Stalks, and established the ritual of the Five Offices and Three Yong at the Stone Channel.

sentences.zh: 乃卜瀍西，爰謀洛食，辨方面勢，仰稟神謀，敷土浚川，為民立極。

translations.literal: Then he divined west of the Chan River, and there sought the sustenance of Luo, distinguishing the directions and terrain, looking up to receive divine counsel, spreading earth and dredging rivers, and establishing the standard for the people.
translations.idiomatic: He divined west of the Chan River and sought the sustenance of Luo, discerning the directions and terrain, looking up to receive divine counsel, spreading earth and dredging rivers, and establishing the standard for the people.

sentences.zh: 兼聿遵先言，表置明堂，爰詔下臣，占星揆日。

translations.literal: Moreover he followed the earlier words and proposed establishing the Bright Hall; then he decreed that your subject below should observe the stars and measure the day.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, following the earlier pronouncement, he proposed establishing the Bright Hall and decreed that your subject below should observe the stars and choose the day.

sentences.zh: 於是采崧山之秘簡，披汶水之靈圖，訪通議於殘亡，購《冬官》於散逸。

translations.literal: Thereupon he gathered the secret bamboo slips of Mount Song, unfolded the numinous charts of the Wen River, sought comprehensive discussions among the damaged and lost, and purchased the "Officer of Winter" from scattered and missing texts.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon I gathered the secret bamboo slips of Mount Song, unfolded the numinous charts of the Wen River, sought out comprehensive discussions among damaged and lost texts, and purchased copies of the "Officer of Winter" from scattered sources.

sentences.zh: 總集眾論，勒成一家。

translations.literal: He gathered all discussions together and carved them into one school.
translations.idiomatic: I gathered all the various opinions together and compiled them into one unified account.

sentences.zh: 昔張衡渾象，以三分為一度，裴秀輿地，以二寸為千里。

translations.literal: Formerly Zhang Heng's armillary sphere used one third as one degree; Pei Xiu's terrestrial map used two inches for one thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Zhang Heng's armillary sphere used one third of a unit for one degree, and Pei Xiu's terrestrial map used two inches for one thousand li.

sentences.zh: 臣之此圖，用一分為一尺，推而演之，冀輪奐有序。

translations.literal: Your subject's present diagram uses one fen as one chi, extending and developing it, hoping that the revolving splendor may have order.
translations.idiomatic: In the present diagram, your subject uses one fen as one chi, extending and developing the design in the hope that the revolving structure may have proper order.

sentences.zh: 而經構之旨，議者殊途，或以綺井為重屋，或以圓楣為隆棟，各以臆說，事不經見。

translations.literal: But on the essential meaning of planning and construction, debaters took different paths: some took patterned wells as double-roofed halls, others took round beams as towering pillars — each relying on personal speculation, matters not verified by experience.
translations.idiomatic: But on the essential meaning of planning and construction, debaters took different paths: some took patterned ceiling wells as double-roofed halls, others took round beams as towering pillars — each relying on personal speculation, with no basis in verified precedent.

sentences.zh: 今錄其疑難，為之通釋，皆出證據，以相發明。

translations.literal: Now I record their doubts and difficulties and provide a thorough explanation for them, all based on evidence, to illuminate one another.
translations.idiomatic: I now record their doubts and difficulties and provide thorough explanations, all grounded in evidence, to clarify one another.

sentences.zh: 議曰：

translations.literal: The discussion says:
translations.idiomatic: The discussion reads:

sentences.zh: :臣愷謹案《淮南子》曰：「昔者神農之治天下也，甘雨以時，五穀蕃植，春生夏長，秋收冬藏，月省時考，終歲獻貢，以時嘗谷，祀於明堂。

translations.literal: Your subject Kai respectfully cites the Huainanzi, which says: "In antiquity when Shennong governed the realm, sweet rain came in season, the five grains flourished and were planted, spring generated and summer grew, autumn harvested and winter stored; monthly inspection and seasonal examination — at year's end tribute was presented, grain was tasted in season, and sacrifice was performed in the Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject Kai respectfully cites the Huainanzi, which says: "In antiquity, when Shennong governed the realm, sweet rain came in season and the five grains flourished. Spring generated, summer grew, autumn harvested, and winter stored. With monthly inspection and seasonal examination, tribute was presented at year's end, grain was tasted in season, and sacrifice was performed in the Bright Hall.

sentences.zh: 明堂之制，有蓋而無四方，風雨不能襲，燥濕不能傷，遷延而入之。」

translations.literal: The institution of the Bright Hall had a covering but no four sides; wind and rain could not penetrate it, dryness and dampness could not harm it, and one entered it by winding around."
translations.idiomatic: The Bright Hall was built with a covering but no four walls, so wind and rain could not penetrate it and dryness and dampness could not harm it; one entered by winding around."

sentences.zh: 臣愷以為上古樸略，創立典刑。

translations.literal: Your subject Kai considers that in high antiquity things were plain and simple, and canonical forms were first established.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject Kai considers that in high antiquity things were plain and simple, and canonical forms were first established.

sentences.zh: 《尚書帝命驗》曰：「帝者承天立五府，以尊天重象。

translations.literal: The Shangshu Di Ming Yan says: "The Emperor, receiving Heaven, establishes the Five Offices to honor Heaven and respect the signs.
translations.idiomatic: The Shangshu Di Ming Yan says: "The Emperor, receiving Heaven, establishes the Five Offices to honor Heaven and respect the celestial signs.

sentences.zh: 赤曰文祖，黃曰神鬥，白曰顯紀，黑曰玄矩，蒼曰靈府。」

translations.literal: The red is called Wen Zu, the yellow is called Shen Dou, the white is called Xian Ji, the black is called Xuan Ju, and the azure is called Ling Fu."
translations.idiomatic: The red is called Wen Zu, the yellow Shen Dou, the white Xian Ji, the black Xuan Ju, and the azure Ling Fu."

sentences.zh: 注雲：「唐、虞之天府，夏之世室，殷之重屋，周之明堂，皆同矣。」

translations.literal: The commentary says: "The Heavenly Office of Tang and Yu, the Generational Chamber of Xia, the Double-Roofed Hall of Yin, and the Bright Hall of Zhou are all the same."
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says: "The Heavenly Office of Tang and Yu, the Generational Chamber of Xia, the Double-Roofed Hall of Yin, and the Bright Hall of Zhou are all the same."

sentences.zh: 《屍子》曰：「有虞氏曰總章。」

translations.literal: The Shizi says: "The Youyu clan called it Zongzhang."
translations.idiomatic: The Shizi says: "The Youyu clan called it Zongzhang."

sentences.zh: 《周官·考工記》曰：「夏後氏世室，堂修二七，博四修一。」

translations.literal: The Zhouguan · Kaogongji says: "The Generational Chamber of the Xia dynasty: the hall's length is two times seven, its width four plus one seventh of the length."
translations.idiomatic: The Zhouguan · Kaogongji says: "The Generational Chamber of the Xia dynasty: the hall's length is two times seven, its width four plus one seventh of the length."

sentences.zh: 注雲：「修南北之深也。

translations.literal: The commentary says: "Xiu is the depth from north to south.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says: "Xiu refers to the depth from north to south.

sentences.zh: 夏度以步，今修十四步，其博益以四分修之一，則明堂博十七步半也。」

translations.literal: Xia measurements used paces; now the length is fourteen paces, and the width is increased by one fourth of the length, so the Bright Hall's width is seventeen and a half paces."
translations.idiomatic: The Xia used paces as their unit of measure; if the length is fourteen paces and the width is increased by one fourth of the length, then the Bright Hall's width would be seventeen and a half paces."

sentences.zh: 臣愷按，三王之世，夏最為古，從質尚文，理應漸就寬大，何因夏室乃大殷堂？

translations.literal: Your subject Kai observes that among the Three Dynasties, Xia was the most ancient; moving from substance toward refinement, it should logically have gradually become broader — why then would the Xia chamber be larger than the Yin hall?
translations.idiomatic: Your subject Kai observes that among the Three Dynasties, Xia was the most ancient; as culture moved from substance toward refinement, halls should logically have grown gradually broader. Why then would the Xia chamber be larger than the Yin hall?

sentences.zh: 相形為論，理恐不爾。

translations.literal: Comparing forms as a basis for argument, the principle probably is not so.
translations.idiomatic: Judging by comparative form, the principle probably does not work that way.

sentences.zh: 《記》雲「堂修七，博四修一」，若夏度以步，則應修七步。

translations.literal: The Record says "the hall's length is seven, its width four plus one seventh of the length"; if Xia measurements used paces, then the length should be seven paces.
translations.idiomatic: The Record says "the hall's length is seven, its width four plus one seventh of the length"; if Xia measurements used paces, then the length should be seven paces.

sentences.zh: 注雲「今堂修十四步」，乃是增益《記》文。

translations.literal: The commentary says "now the hall's length is fourteen paces" — this is an addition to the text of the Record.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary's statement that "now the hall's length is fourteen paces" is an addition to the text of the Record itself.

sentences.zh: 殷、週二堂獨無加字，便是其義，類例不同。

translations.literal: The Yin and Zhou halls alone have no added characters — this shows their meaning; the categories and examples differ.
translations.idiomatic: The Yin and Zhou entries alone contain no added characters, which shows the point: the categories and examples differ.

sentences.zh: 山東《禮》本輒加二七之字，何得殷無加尋之文，周闕增筵之義？

translations.literal: The Shandong edition of the Ritual text arbitrarily adds the characters for "two seven"; how can it be that Yin has no added text for xun, and Zhou lacks added meaning for mats?
translations.idiomatic: The Shandong edition of the Ritual text arbitrarily adds the characters for "two seven"; how can it be that the Yin entry has no added text for xun, and the Zhou entry lacks added meaning for mats?

sentences.zh: 研核其趣，或是不然。

translations.literal: Examining and verifying its purport, perhaps it is not so.
translations.idiomatic: On closer examination of its purport, perhaps it is not so.

sentences.zh: 讎校古書，並無二字，此乃桑間俗儒信情加減。

translations.literal: Collating ancient books, there are no two characters at all; this is simply a vulgar scholar of Sangjian adding and subtracting at will.
translations.idiomatic: Collating ancient books, there are no such two characters at all; this is simply a vulgar scholar adding and subtracting at will.

sentences.zh: 《黃圖議》雲：「夏後氏益其堂之大一百四十四尺，周人明堂以為兩杼間。」

translations.literal: The Huangtu Yi says: "The Xia dynasty enlarged its hall by one hundred forty-four chi; the Zhou people's Bright Hall used this as the space between two tie-beams."
translations.idiomatic: The Huangtu Yi says: "The Xia dynasty enlarged its hall by one hundred forty-four chi; the Zhou people's Bright Hall used this as the space between two tie-beams."

sentences.zh: 馬宮之言，止論堂之一面，據此為准，則三代堂基並方，得為上圓之制。

translations.literal: Ma Gong's words discuss only one face of the hall; taking this as the standard, then the hall foundations of the Three Dynasties were all square, which would allow the institution of round above and square below.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Gong's words discuss only one face of the hall; taking this as the standard, the hall foundations of the Three Dynasties were all square, which would allow the round-above, square-below design.

sentences.zh: 諸書所說，並雲下方，鄭注《周官》，獨為此義，非直與古違異，亦乃乖背禮文。

translations.literal: All the books say square below; Zheng's commentary on the Zhouguan alone holds this meaning — it not only directly differs from antiquity, but also violates the ritual text.
translations.idiomatic: All the books say square below; Zheng's commentary on the Zhouguan alone holds this meaning — it not only directly differs from antiquity, but also violates the ritual text.

sentences.zh: 尋文求理，深恐未愜。

translations.literal: Searching the text and seeking the principle, I deeply fear it is not satisfactory.
translations.idiomatic: Searching the text and seeking the principle, I deeply fear it is not satisfactory.

sentences.zh: 《屍子》曰：「殷人陽館。」

translations.literal: The Shizi says: "The Yin people [called it] the Yang Hall."
translations.idiomatic: The Shizi says: "The Yin people called it the Yang Hall."

sentences.zh: 《考工記》曰：「殷人重屋，堂修七尋，堂崇三尺，四阿重屋。」

translations.literal: The Kaogongji says: "The Yin people's Double-Roofed Hall: the hall's length is seven xun, the hall's height three chi, with four eaves and double roofs."
translations.idiomatic: The Kaogongji says: "The Yin people's Double-Roofed Hall: the hall's length is seven xun, the hall's height three chi, with four eaves and double roofs."

sentences.zh: 注雲：其修七尋，五丈六尺，放夏周則其博九尋，七丈二尺。」

translations.literal: The commentary says: its length seven xun is five zhang six chi; following Xia and Zhou, its width would be nine xun, seven zhang two chi."
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says: its length of seven xun equals five zhang six chi; following the Xia and Zhou proportions, its width would be nine xun, seven zhang two chi."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「周人明堂，度九尺之筵，東西九筵。

translations.literal: It also says: "The Zhou people's Bright Hall: using the nine-chi mat as the unit, nine mats east to west.
translations.idiomatic: It also says: "The Zhou people's Bright Hall: using the nine-chi mat as the unit, nine mats east to west.

sentences.zh: 南北七筵。

translations.literal: Seven mats north to south.
translations.idiomatic: Seven mats north to south.

sentences.zh: 堂崇一筵。

translations.literal: The hall's height one mat.
translations.idiomatic: The hall's height one mat.

sentences.zh: 五室，凡二筵。」

translations.literal: The five chambers, altogether two mats."
translations.idiomatic: The five chambers, altogether two mats."

sentences.zh: 《禮記·明堂位》曰：「天子之廟，複廟重簷。」

translations.literal: The Liji · Mingtangwei says: "The Son of Heaven's temple has double eaves and layered roofs."
translations.idiomatic: The Liji · Mingtangwei says: "The Son of Heaven's temple has double eaves and layered roofs."

sentences.zh: 鄭注雲：「複廟，重屋也。」

translations.literal: Zheng's commentary says: "Double temple means double-roofed hall."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng's commentary says: "Double temple means double-roofed hall."

sentences.zh: 注《玉藻》雲：「天子廟及露寢，皆如明堂制。」

translations.literal: The commentary on Yuzao says: "The Son of Heaven's temple and open sleeping hall are both like the Bright Hall institution."
translations.idiomatic: The commentary on Yuzao says: "The Son of Heaven's temple and open sleeping hall both follow the Bright Hall design."

sentences.zh: 《禮圖》雲：「于內室之上，起通天之觀，觀八十一尺，得宮之數，其聲濁，君之象也。」

translations.literal: The Litu says: "Above the inner chambers, a tower reaching to Heaven is raised; the tower is eighty-one chi, obtaining the number of the Gong pitch — its sound is low, the image of the ruler."
translations.idiomatic: The Litu says: "Above the inner chambers, a tower reaching to Heaven is raised; the tower is eighty-one chi, obtaining the number of the Gong pitch — its sound is low, the image of the ruler."

sentences.zh: 《大戴禮》曰：「明堂者，古有之。

translations.literal: The Dadai Li says: "The Bright Hall — antiquity had it.
translations.idiomatic: The Dadai Li says: "The Bright Hall existed in antiquity.

sentences.zh: 凡九室，一室有四戶八牖。

translations.literal: Altogether nine chambers; each chamber had four doors and eight windows.
translations.idiomatic: There were nine chambers in all; each chamber had four doors and eight windows.

sentences.zh: 以茅蓋，上圓下方，外水曰璧雝。

translations.literal: It was thatched with reeds, round above and square below; the outer water was called Biyong.
translations.idiomatic: It was thatched with reeds, round above and square below; the outer moat was called Biyong.

sentences.zh: 赤綴戶，白綴牖。

translations.literal: Red trim on the doors, white trim on the windows.
translations.idiomatic: Red trim adorned the doors, white trim the windows.

sentences.zh: 堂高三尺，東西九仞，南北七筵。

translations.literal: The hall was three chi high, nine ren east to west, seven mats north to south.
translations.idiomatic: The hall was three chi high, nine ren east to west, and seven mats north to south.

sentences.zh: 其宮方三百步。

translations.literal: Its precinct was three hundred paces square.
translations.idiomatic: Its precinct was three hundred paces square.

sentences.zh: 凡人民疾，六畜疫，五穀災，生於天道不順。

translations.literal: Whenever the people fell ill, livestock suffered plague, or the five grains met disaster, it arose from Heaven's Way being unbalanced.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the people fell ill, livestock suffered plague, or the five grains met disaster, it arose from Heaven's Way being out of balance.

sentences.zh: 天道不順，生於明堂不飾。

translations.literal: Heaven's Way being unbalanced arose from the Bright Hall not being adorned.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's Way being out of balance arose from the Bright Hall not being properly adorned.

sentences.zh: 故有天災，則飾明堂。」

translations.literal: Therefore when there was a heavenly disaster, the Bright Hall was adorned."
translations.idiomatic: Therefore when heavenly disaster struck, the Bright Hall was adorned."

sentences.zh: 《周書·明堂》曰：「堂方百一十二尺，高四尺，階博六尺三寸。

translations.literal: The Zhou Shu · Mingtang says: "The hall was one hundred twelve chi square, four chi high, with steps six chi three inches wide.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou Shu · Mingtang says: "The hall was one hundred twelve chi square, four chi high, with steps six chi three inches wide.

sentences.zh: 室居內，方百尺，室內方六十尺。

translations.literal: The chambers were inside, one hundred chi square; the inner chamber space was sixty chi square.
translations.idiomatic: The chambers were inside, one hundred chi square; the inner chamber space was sixty chi square.

sentences.zh: 戶高八尺，博四尺。」

translations.literal: The doors were eight chi high and four chi wide."
translations.idiomatic: The doors were eight chi high and four chi wide."

sentences.zh: 《作洛》曰：「明堂太廟露寢，咸有四阿，重亢重廊。」

translations.literal: The Zuo Luo says: "The Bright Hall, Grand Temple, and Open Sleeping Hall all had four eaves, layered rafters and layered corridors."
translations.idiomatic: The Zuo Luo says: "The Bright Hall, Grand Temple, and Open Sleeping Hall all had four eaves, layered rafters and layered corridors."

sentences.zh: 孔氏注雲：「重亢累棟，重廊累屋也。」

translations.literal: Kong's commentary says: "Layered rafters are accumulated ridgepoles; layered corridors are accumulated roofs."
translations.idiomatic: Kong's commentary says: "Layered rafters mean accumulated ridgepoles; layered corridors mean accumulated roofs."

sentences.zh: 《禮圖》曰：「秦明堂九室十二階，各有所居。」

translations.literal: The Litu says: "The Qin Bright Hall had nine chambers and twelve steps, each with its assigned place."
translations.idiomatic: The Litu says: "The Qin Bright Hall had nine chambers and twelve steps, each with its assigned place."

sentences.zh: :《呂氏春秋》曰：「有十二堂。」

translations.literal: The Lüshi Chunqiu says: "There are twelve halls."
translations.idiomatic: The Lüshi Chunqiu says: "There are twelve halls."

sentences.zh: 與《月令》同，並不論尺丈。

translations.literal: It agrees with the Yueling, and neither discusses measurements in chi and zhang.
translations.idiomatic: It agrees with the Yueling, and neither discusses measurements in chi and zhang.

sentences.zh: 臣愷案，十二階雖不與《禮》合，一月一階，非無理思。

translations.literal: Your subject Kai observes that although twelve steps do not accord with the Ritual, one step per month is not without rational thought.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject Kai observes that although twelve steps do not accord with the Ritual, one step per month is not without rational thought.

sentences.zh: 《黃圖》曰：「堂方百四十四尺，法坤之策也，方象地。

translations.literal: The Huangtu says: "The hall is one hundred forty-four chi square, following the tally of Kun — square, symbolizing Earth.
translations.idiomatic: The Huangtu says: "The hall is one hundred forty-four chi square, following the tally of Kun — square, symbolizing Earth.

sentences.zh: 屋圓楣徑二百一十六尺，法乾之策也，圓象天。

translations.literal: The roof's round beam has a diameter of two hundred sixteen chi, following the tally of Qian — round, symbolizing Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The roof's round beam has a diameter of two hundred sixteen chi, following the tally of Qian — round, symbolizing Heaven.

sentences.zh: 太室九宮，法九州。

translations.literal: The Grand Chamber's nine palaces follow the Nine Provinces.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Chamber's nine palaces follow the Nine Provinces.

sentences.zh: 太室方六丈，法陰之變數。

translations.literal: The Grand Chamber is six zhang square, following the changing numbers of yin.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Chamber is six zhang square, following the changing numbers of yin.

sentences.zh: 十二堂法十二月，三十六戶法極陰之變數，七十二牖法五行所行日數。

translations.literal: The twelve halls follow the twelve months; the thirty-six doors follow the changing numbers of ultimate yin; the seventy-two windows follow the days of the Five Phases' movement.
translations.idiomatic: The twelve halls follow the twelve months; the thirty-six doors follow the changing numbers of ultimate yin; the seventy-two windows follow the days of the Five Phases' movement.

sentences.zh: 八達象八風，法八卦。

translations.literal: The eight thoroughfares symbolize the eight winds, following the Eight Trigrams.
translations.idiomatic: The eight thoroughfares symbolize the eight winds, following the Eight Trigrams.

sentences.zh: 通天台徑九尺，法乾以九覆六。

translations.literal: The Tower Reaching Heaven has a diameter of nine chi, following Qian's nine covering six.
translations.idiomatic: The Tower Reaching Heaven has a diameter of nine chi, following Qian's nine covering six.

sentences.zh: 高八十一尺，法黃鐘九九之數。

translations.literal: Its height is eighty-one chi, following the number of Yellow Bell's nine times nine.
translations.idiomatic: Its height is eighty-one chi, following the number of Yellow Bell's nine times nine.

sentences.zh: 二十八柱象二十八宿。

translations.literal: The twenty-eight pillars symbolize the twenty-eight lunar mansions.
translations.idiomatic: The twenty-eight pillars symbolize the twenty-eight lunar mansions.

sentences.zh: 堂高三尺，上階三等，法三統。

translations.literal: The hall is three chi high, with three upper steps, following the Three Successions.
translations.idiomatic: The hall is three chi high, with three upper steps, following the Three Successions.

sentences.zh: 堂四向五色，法四時五行。

translations.literal: The hall faces four directions in five colors, following the four seasons and Five Phases.
translations.idiomatic: The hall faces four directions in five colors, following the four seasons and Five Phases.

sentences.zh: 殿門去殿七十二步，法五行所行。

translations.literal: The palace gate is seventy-two paces from the palace, following the movement of the Five Phases.
translations.idiomatic: The palace gate is seventy-two paces from the palace, following the movement of the Five Phases.

sentences.zh: 門堂長四丈，取太室三之二。

translations.literal: The gate hall is four zhang long, taking two thirds of the Grand Chamber.
translations.idiomatic: The gate hall is four zhang long, taking two thirds of the Grand Chamber.

sentences.zh: 垣高無蔽目之照，牖六尺，其外倍之。

translations.literal: The wall's height does not block the eye's view; windows are six chi, and outside them the distance is doubled.
translations.idiomatic: The wall's height does not block the eye's view; windows are six chi, and outside them the distance is doubled.

sentences.zh: 殿垣方，在水內，法地陰也。

translations.literal: The palace wall is square, inside the water, following Earth's yin.
translations.idiomatic: The palace wall is square, inside the water, following Earth's yin.

sentences.zh: 水四周于外，象四海，圓法陽也。

translations.literal: Water surrounds it on all four sides outside, symbolizing the four seas; round follows yang.
translations.idiomatic: Water surrounds it on all four sides outside, symbolizing the four seas; round follows yang.

sentences.zh: 水闊二十四丈，象二十四氣。

translations.literal: The water is twenty-four zhang wide, symbolizing the twenty-four qi.
translations.idiomatic: The water is twenty-four zhang wide, symbolizing the twenty-four qi.

sentences.zh: 水內徑三丈，應《覲禮經》。」

translations.literal: The inner diameter of the water is three zhang, corresponding to the Jingli Jing."
translations.idiomatic: The inner diameter of the water is three zhang, corresponding to the Jingli Jing."

sentences.zh: 武帝元封二年，立明堂汶上，無室。

translations.literal: In Yuanfeng 2 under Emperor Wu, the Bright Hall was established at Wenshang, without chambers.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Wu's Yuanfeng 2, the Bright Hall was built at Wenshang without chambers.

sentences.zh: 其外略依此制。

translations.literal: Its exterior roughly followed this design.
translations.idiomatic: Its exterior roughly followed this design.

sentences.zh: 《泰山通議》今亡，不可得而辨也。

translations.literal: The Taishan Tongyi is now lost and cannot be examined and distinguished.
translations.idiomatic: The Taishan Tongyi is now lost and cannot be examined and distinguished.

sentences.zh: :八月，起明堂、辟雍長安城南門，制度如儀。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, the Bright Hall and Imperial Academy were begun at the south gate of Chang'an city, with institutions according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, the Bright Hall and Imperial Academy were begun at the south gate of Chang'an city, with institutions according to ritual.

sentences.zh: 一殿，垣四面，門八觀，水外周，堤壤高四尺，和會築作三旬。

translations.literal: One hall, walls on four sides, eight gates and towers, water surrounding outside, embankments four chi high; the combined construction took thirty days.
translations.idiomatic: One hall, walls on four sides, eight gates and towers, water surrounding outside, embankments four chi high; the combined construction took thirty days.

sentences.zh: 五年正月六日辛未，始郊太祖高皇帝以配天。

translations.literal: On the sixth day of the first month of the fifth year, xinwei, he first performed suburban sacrifice to the Grand Ancestor Emperor Gao, with him as companion to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: On the sixth day of the first month of the fifth year, xinwei, he first performed suburban sacrifice to the Grand Ancestor Emperor Gao, with him as companion to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 二十二日丁亥，宗祀孝文皇帝于明堂以配上帝，及先賢、百辟、卿士有益者，於是秩而祭之。

translations.literal: On the twenty-second day, dinghai, he performed ancestral sacrifice to Emperor Xiaowen in the Bright Hall as companion to the Supreme Lord, and also to worthy sages of old, the hundred officials, and ministers who had been beneficial — thereupon ranking them and sacrificing to them.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-second day, dinghai, he performed ancestral sacrifice to Emperor Xiaowen in the Bright Hall as companion to the Supreme Lord, and also to worthy sages of old, the hundred officials, and ministers who had been beneficial — thereupon ranking them and sacrificing to them.

sentences.zh: 親扶三老五更，袒而割牲，跪而進之。

translations.literal: He personally supported the Three Elders and Five More Venerable Ones, bared his shoulder and cut the sacrificial victim, knelt and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: He personally supported the Three Elders and Five More Venerable Ones, bared his shoulder and cut the sacrificial victim, knelt and presented it.

sentences.zh: 因班時令，宣恩澤。

translations.literal: Thereupon he distributed the seasonal commands and proclaimed grace and favor.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he distributed the seasonal commands and proclaimed grace and favor.

sentences.zh: 諸侯王、宗室、四夷君長、匈奴、西國侍子，悉奉貢助祭。

translations.literal: Princes, imperial clansmen, chieftains of the four barbarians, the Xiongnu, and hostages from western states all presented tribute and assisted in the sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Princes, imperial clansmen, chieftains of the four barbarians, the Xiongnu, and hostages from western states all presented tribute and assisted in the sacrifice.

sentences.zh: :《禮圖》曰：「作明堂，明堂上圓下方，上圓法天，下方法地，十二堂法日辰，九室法九州。

translations.literal: The Litu says: "In building the Bright Hall, the Bright Hall is round above and square below — round above follows Heaven, square below follows Earth; twelve halls follow the day-stars, nine chambers follow the Nine Provinces.
translations.idiomatic: The Litu says: "In building the Bright Hall, the Bright Hall is round above and square below — round above follows Heaven, square below follows Earth; twelve halls follow the day-stars, nine chambers follow the Nine Provinces.

sentences.zh: 室八牖，八九七十二，法一時之王。

translations.literal: Each chamber has eight windows; eight times nine is seventy-two, following the king of one season.
translations.idiomatic: Each chamber has eight windows; eight times nine is seventy-two, following the king of one season.

sentences.zh: 室有二戶，二九十八戶，法土王十八日。

translations.literal: Each chamber has two doors; two times nine is eighteen doors, following Earth's eighteen days of kingship.
translations.idiomatic: Each chamber has two doors; two times nine is eighteen doors, following Earth's eighteen days of kingship.

sentences.zh: 內堂正壇高三尺，土階三等。」

translations.literal: The inner hall's central altar is three chi high, with three earthen steps."
translations.idiomatic: The inner hall's central altar is three chi high, with three earthen steps."

sentences.zh: 胡伯始注《漢官》雲：「古清廟蓋以茅，今蓋以瓦，瓦下藉茅，以存古制。」

translations.literal: Hu Boshi's commentary on the Hangguan says: "In antiquity the Pure Temple was thatched with reeds; now it is covered with tiles, with reeds placed beneath the tiles to preserve the ancient institution."
translations.idiomatic: Hu Boshi's commentary on the Hangguan says: "In antiquity the Pure Temple was thatched with reeds; now it is covered with tiles, with reeds placed beneath the tiles to preserve the ancient institution."

sentences.zh: 《東京賦》曰：「乃營三宮，布政頒常。

translations.literal: The Dongjing Fu says: "Then the three palaces were built, government was dispensed and regular laws proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: The Dongjing Fu says: "Then the three palaces were built, government was dispensed and regular laws proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 複廟重屋，八達九房。

translations.literal: Double temples and layered roofs, eight thoroughfares and nine chambers.
translations.idiomatic: Double temples and layered roofs, eight thoroughfares and nine chambers.

sentences.zh: 造舟清池，惟水泱泱。」

translations.literal: Boats were built on the clear pool, and the waters flowed wide."
translations.idiomatic: Boats were built on the clear pool, and the waters flowed wide."

sentences.zh: 薛綜注雲：「複重廇覆，謂屋平覆重棟也。」

translations.literal: Xue Zong's commentary says: "Double layered covering means the roof flatly covers with double ridgepoles."
translations.idiomatic: Xue Zong's commentary says: "Double layered covering means the roof flatly covers with double ridgepoles."

sentences.zh: 《續漢書·祭祀志》雲：「明帝，祀五帝於明堂，五帝坐各處其方，黃帝在未，皆如南郊之位。

translations.literal: The Xu Hanshu · Jisi Zhi says: "Emperor Ming sacrificed to the Five Emperors in the Bright Hall; the Five Emperors each sat in their direction, the Yellow Emperor at wei — all as at the southern suburb positions.
translations.idiomatic: The Xu Hanshu · Jisi Zhi says: "Emperor Ming sacrificed to the Five Emperors in the Bright Hall; the Five Emperors each sat in their direction, the Yellow Emperor at wei — all as at the southern suburb positions.

sentences.zh: 光武位在青帝之南，少退西面，各一犢，奏樂如南郊。」

translations.literal: Emperor Guangwu's seat was south of the Green Emperor, slightly withdrawn to the west; each had one calf, and music was performed as at the southern suburb."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Guangwu's seat was south of the Green Emperor, slightly withdrawn to the west; each had one calf, and music was performed as at the southern suburb."

sentences.zh: 臣愷按《詩》雲，《我將》祀文王於明堂，「我將我享，維牛維羊」。

translations.literal: Your subject Kai cites the Shi, which says in "Wo Jiang" that King Wen was sacrificed to in the Bright Hall: "I will offer, I will enjoy — only oxen and sheep."
translations.idiomatic: Your subject Kai cites the Shi, which says in "Wo Jiang" that King Wen was sacrificed to in the Bright Hall: "I will offer, I will enjoy — only oxen and sheep."

sentences.zh: 據此則備太牢之祭。

translations.literal: According to this, the complete tai lao sacrifice was prepared.
translations.idiomatic: According to this, the complete tai lao sacrifice was prepared.

sentences.zh: 今雲一犢，恐與古殊。

translations.literal: Now it says one calf — I fear this differs from antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Now it says one calf — I fear this differs from antiquity.

sentences.zh: 自晉以前，未有鶉尾，其圓牆璧水，一依本圖。

translations.literal: Before the Jin, there was no Chunwei; the round wall and jade-ring water all followed the original diagram.
translations.idiomatic: Before the Jin, there was no Chunwei; the round wall and jade-ring water all followed the original diagram.

sentences.zh: 《晉起居注》裴頠議曰：「尊祖配天，其義明著，廟宇之制，理據未分。

translations.literal: The Jin Qiju Zhu: Pei Yi argued: "Honoring the ancestor as companion to Heaven — its meaning is clear and evident; but the institution of the temple's structure, its principles and evidence, are not yet distinguished.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin Qiju Zhu: Pei Yi argued: "Honoring the ancestor as companion to Heaven — its meaning is clear and evident; but the institution of the temple's structure, its principles and evidence, are not yet distinguished.

sentences.zh: 直可為一殿，以崇嚴祀，其餘雜碎，一皆除之。」

translations.literal: One may simply make one hall to elevate solemn sacrifice; all other miscellaneous elements should be entirely removed."
translations.idiomatic: One may simply make one hall to elevate solemn sacrifice; all other miscellaneous elements should be entirely removed."

sentences.zh: 臣愷案，天垂象，聖人則之。

translations.literal: Your subject Kai observes that Heaven displays signs, and the sage follows them.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject Kai observes that Heaven displays signs, and the sage follows them.

sentences.zh: 辟雍之星，既有圖狀，晉堂方構，不合天文。

translations.literal: The star of the Imperial Academy already had a diagram; the Jin hall was built square, not conforming to celestial patterns.
translations.idiomatic: The star of the Imperial Academy already had a diagram; the Jin hall was built square, not conforming to celestial patterns.

sentences.zh: 既闕重樓，又無璧水，空堂乖五室之義，直殿違九階之文。

translations.literal: It lacked layered towers, and also had no jade-ring water; an empty hall violated the meaning of five chambers, and a straight hall violated the text of nine steps.
translations.idiomatic: It lacked layered towers, and also had no jade-ring water; an empty hall violated the meaning of five chambers, and a straight hall violated the text of nine steps.

sentences.zh: 非古欺天，一何過甚！

translations.literal: Deviating from antiquity and deceiving Heaven — how excessive!
translations.idiomatic: Deviating from antiquity and deceiving Heaven — how excessive!

sentences.zh: 後魏于北台城南造圓牆，在璧水外，門在水內迥立，不與牆相連。

translations.literal: Later Wei built a round wall south of Beitai city, outside the jade-ring water; the gates stood separately inside the water, not connected to the wall.
translations.idiomatic: Later Wei built a round wall south of Beitai city, outside the jade-ring water; the gates stood separately inside the water, not connected to the wall.

sentences.zh: 其堂上九室，三三相重，不依古制，室間通巷，違舛處多。

translations.literal: Above the hall were nine chambers, three by three overlapping; it did not follow the ancient institution, and passages ran between chambers — there were many violations.
translations.idiomatic: Above the hall were nine chambers, three by three overlapping; it did not follow the ancient institution, and passages ran between chambers — there were many violations.

sentences.zh: 其室皆用墼累，極成褊陋。

translations.literal: All its chambers were built up with bricks, becoming extremely cramped and crude.
translations.idiomatic: All its chambers were built up with bricks, becoming extremely cramped and crude.

sentences.zh: 後魏《樂志》曰：「立明堂，議者或言九室，或言五室，詔斷從五室。

translations.literal: The Later Wei Yue Zhi says: "In establishing the Bright Hall, debaters said either nine chambers or five chambers; an edict decided on five chambers.
translations.idiomatic: The Later Wei Yue Zhi says: "In establishing the Bright Hall, debaters said either nine chambers or five chambers; an edict decided on five chambers.

sentences.zh: 後元叉執政，複改為九室，遭亂不成。」

translations.literal: Later when Yuan Cha held power, it was changed back to nine chambers, but chaos prevented completion."
translations.idiomatic: Later when Yuan Cha held power, it was changed back to nine chambers, but chaos prevented completion."

sentences.zh: 《宋起居注》曰：「孝武帝立明堂，其牆宇規範，擬則太廟，唯十二間，以應期數。

translations.literal: The Song Qiju Zhu says: "Emperor Xiaowu of Song established the Bright Hall; its walls and structure were modeled on the Grand Temple, with only twelve bays to correspond to the cycle of numbers.
translations.idiomatic: The Song Qiju Zhu says: "Emperor Xiaowu of Song established the Bright Hall; its walls and structure were modeled on the Grand Temple, with only twelve bays to correspond to the cycle of numbers.

sentences.zh: 依漢《汶上圖儀》，設五帝位。

translations.literal: Following the Han Wenshang Tuyi, seats for the Five Emperors were set up.
translations.idiomatic: Following the Han Wenshang Tuyi, seats for the Five Emperors were set up.

sentences.zh: 太祖文皇帝對饗，鼎俎簠簋，一依廟禮。」

translations.literal: Grand Ancestor Emperor Wen was paired in the feast; tripods, stands, and grain vessels all followed temple ritual."
translations.idiomatic: Grand Ancestor Emperor Wen was paired in the feast; tripods, stands, and grain vessels all followed temple ritual."

sentences.zh: 梁武即位之後，移宋時太極殿以為明堂。

translations.literal: After Emperor Wu of Liang succeeded to the throne, he moved the Song-era Hall of Supreme Ultimate to serve as the Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Wu of Liang succeeded to the throne, he moved the Song-era Hall of Supreme Ultimate to serve as the Bright Hall.

sentences.zh: 無室，十二間。

translations.literal: It had no chambers, only twelve bays.
translations.idiomatic: It had no chambers, only twelve bays.

sentences.zh: 《禮疑議》雲：「祭用純漆俎瓦樽，文於郊，質於廟。

translations.literal: The Li Yiyi says: "In sacrifice, pure lacquer stands and earthenware goblets were used — refined at the suburb, plain at the temple.
translations.idiomatic: The Li Yiyi says: "In sacrifice, pure lacquer stands and earthenware goblets were used — refined at the suburb, plain at the temple.

sentences.zh: 止一獻，用清酒。」

translations.literal: Only one presentation, using clear wine."
translations.idiomatic: Only one presentation, using clear wine."

sentences.zh: 平陳之後，臣得目觀，遂量步數，記其尺丈。

translations.literal: After the pacification of Chen, your subject was able to see it with his own eyes, and thereupon measured the paces and recorded its dimensions in chi and zhang.
translations.idiomatic: After the pacification of Chen, your subject was able to see it with his own eyes, and thereupon measured the paces and recorded its dimensions in chi and zhang.

sentences.zh: 猶見基內有焚燒殘柱，毀斫之餘，入地一丈，儼然如舊。

translations.literal: One could still see within the foundation burned remnant pillars; of what remained after destruction and cutting, one zhang entered the ground, standing as if still intact.
translations.idiomatic: One could still see within the foundation burned remnant pillars; of what remained after destruction and cutting, one zhang entered the ground, standing as if still intact.

sentences.zh: 柱下以樟木為跗，長丈餘，闊四尺許，兩兩相並。

translations.literal: Beneath the pillars camphor wood was used for bases, more than one zhang long and about four chi wide, placed two by two side by side.
translations.idiomatic: Beneath the pillars camphor wood was used for bases, more than one zhang long and about four chi wide, placed two by two side by side.

sentences.zh: 瓦安數重。

translations.literal: Tiles were placed in several layers.
translations.idiomatic: Tiles were placed in several layers.

sentences.zh: 宮城處所，乃在郭內。

translations.literal: The palace city's location was inside the outer wall.
translations.idiomatic: The palace city's location was inside the outer wall.

sentences.zh: 雖湫隘卑陋，未合規摹，祖宗之靈，得崇嚴祀。

translations.literal: Although cramped, low, and crude, not conforming to the standard design, the spirits of the ancestors could still receive elevated and solemn sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Although cramped, low, and crude, not conforming to the standard design, the spirits of the ancestors could still receive elevated and solemn sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 周、齊二代，闕而不修，大饗之典，於焉靡托。

translations.literal: Under the Zhou and Qi dynasties, it was left unrepaired; the great feast ritual had no place to rely upon.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Zhou and Qi dynasties, it was left unrepaired; the great feast ritual had no place to rely upon.

sentences.zh: :自古明堂圖惟有二本，一是宗周，劉熙、阮諶、劉昌宗等作，三圖略同。

translations.literal: From antiquity there have been only two versions of Bright Hall diagrams: one is the Zhou royal house, made by Liu Xi, Ruan Chen, Liu Changzong, and others — the three diagrams are roughly the same.
translations.idiomatic: From antiquity there have been only two versions of Bright Hall diagrams: one is the Zhou royal house version, made by Liu Xi, Ruan Chen, Liu Changzong, and others — the three diagrams are roughly the same.

sentences.zh: 一是後漢作，《禮圖》有本，不詳撰人。

translations.literal: One is a Later Han version; the Litu has a copy, but the author is not known in detail.
translations.idiomatic: One is a Later Han version; the Litu has a copy, but the author is not known in detail.

sentences.zh: 臣遠尋經傳，傍求子史，研究眾說，總撰今圖。

translations.literal: Your subject searched far in the classics and commentaries, sought widely in the masters and histories, studied the various opinions, and compiled the present diagram.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject searched far in the classics and commentaries, sought widely in the masters and histories, studied the various opinions, and compiled the present diagram.

sentences.zh: 其樣以木為之，下為方堂，堂有五室，上為圓觀，觀有四門。

translations.literal: Its model was made of wood: below was a square hall with five chambers; above was a round tower with four gates.
translations.idiomatic: Its model was made of wood: below was a square hall with five chambers; above was a round tower with four gates.

sentences.zh: 帝可其奏。

translations.literal: The emperor approved his memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved his memorial.

sentences.zh: 會遼東之役，事不果行。

translations.literal: It happened that the Liaodong campaign intervened, and the matter was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The Liaodong campaign intervened, and the matter was not carried out.

sentences.zh: 以渡遼之功，進位金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: For his merit in crossing the Liao, he was promoted to Grand Master of Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit in crossing the Liao, he was promoted to Grand Master of Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.

sentences.zh: 其年卒官，時年五十八。

translations.literal: That year he died in office, at age fifty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: That year he died in office, at age fifty-eight.

sentences.zh: 帝甚惜之。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor deeply regretted his loss.

sentences.zh: 諡曰康。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Kang.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous title was Kang.

sentences.zh: 撰《東都圖記》二十卷、《明堂圖議》二卷、《釋疑》一卷，見行於世。

translations.literal: He wrote twenty juan of Records of the Eastern Capital Diagrams, two juan of Discussions on the Bright Hall Diagram, and one juan of Resolving Doubts — all circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote twenty juan of Records of the Eastern Capital Diagrams, two juan of Discussions on the Bright Hall Diagram, and one juan of Resolving Doubts — all circulated in his time.

sentences.zh: 子儒童，游騎尉。

translations.literal: His son Rutong was Commandant of Roaming Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: His son Rutong served as Commandant of Roaming Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 少子溫，起部承務郎。

translations.literal: His youngest son Wen was Attendant of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: His youngest son Wen served as Attendant of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 閻毗，榆林盛樂人也。

translations.literal: Yan Pi, Yan Pi, was a native of Shengle in Yulin.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Pi was a native of Shengle in Yulin.

sentences.zh: 祖進，魏本郡太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Jin was Prefect of the native commandery under Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Jin was Prefect of the native commandery under Wei.

sentences.zh: 父慶，周上柱國、甯州總管。

translations.literal: His father Qing was Senior Pillar of State under Zhou and Area Commander of Ningzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qing was Senior Pillar of State under Zhou and Area Commander of Ningzhou.

sentences.zh: 毗七歲，襲爵石保縣公，邑千戶。

translations.literal: At age seven Pi inherited the title Duke of Shibao County, with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: At age seven Yan Pi inherited the title Duke of Shibao County, with a fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 及長，儀貌矜嚴，頗好經史。

translations.literal: When grown, his bearing and appearance were dignified and stern, and he was quite fond of the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: When grown, his bearing and appearance were dignified and stern, and he was quite fond of the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 受《漢書》于蕭該，略通大旨。

translations.literal: He received the Hanshu from Xiao Gai and gained a general understanding of its main purport.
translations.idiomatic: He studied the Hanshu under Xiao Gai and gained a general understanding of its main purport.

sentences.zh: 能篆書，工草隸，尤善畫，為當時之妙。

translations.literal: He could write seal script, was skilled at cursive and clerical script, and was especially good at painting — the finest of his age.
translations.idiomatic: He could write seal script, was skilled at cursive and clerical script, and was especially good at painting — the finest artist of his age.

sentences.zh: 周武帝見而悅之，命尚清都公主。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Zhou saw him and was pleased, and ordered him to marry Princess Qingdu.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Zhou saw him and was pleased, and ordered him to marry Princess Qingdu.

sentences.zh: 宣帝即位，拜儀同三司，授千牛左右。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan succeeded to the throne, he was appointed Yitong Third Rank and granted the post of Thousand-Ox Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan succeeded to the throne, Yan Pi was appointed Yitong Third Rank and granted the post of Thousand-Ox Guard.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，以技藝侍東宮，數以雕麗之物取悅于皇太子，由是甚見親待，每稱之於上。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen received the abdication, he served the Eastern Palace with his skills and arts, repeatedly pleasing the Crown Prince with ornate and beautiful objects; thereby he was greatly favored and treated with intimacy, and was often praised to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen received the abdication, Yan Pi served the Eastern Palace with his skills and arts, repeatedly pleasing the Crown Prince with ornate and beautiful objects. Thereby he was greatly favored and treated with intimacy, and was often praised to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 尋拜車騎，宿衛東宮。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Chariots and Cavalry and served as night guard of the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed Chariots and Cavalry and served as night guard of the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 上嘗遣高熲大閱于龍台澤，諸軍部伍多不齊整，唯毗一軍法制肅然。

translations.literal: The emperor once sent Gao Jiong to conduct a grand review at Longtai Marsh; the ranks of the various armies were mostly not orderly, but only Pi's army was disciplined and solemn in its regulations.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once sent Gao Jiong to conduct a grand review at Longtai Marsh; the ranks of the various armies were mostly disorderly, but only Yan Pi's army was disciplined and solemn in its regulations.

sentences.zh: 熲言之於上，特蒙賜帛。

translations.literal: Jiong reported this to the emperor, and he specially received a gift of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Jiong reported this to the emperor, and Yan Pi specially received a gift of silk.

sentences.zh: 俄兼太子宗衛率長史，尋加上儀同。

translations.literal: Soon he additionally served as Chief Clerk of the Crown Prince's Palace Guard Command, and soon was promoted to Senior Yitong.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he additionally served as Chief Clerk of the Crown Prince's Palace Guard Command, and soon was promoted to Senior Yitong.

sentences.zh: 太子服玩之物，多毗所為。

translations.literal: Most of the Crown Prince's clothing and playthings were made by Pi.
translations.idiomatic: Most of the Crown Prince's clothing and playthings were made by Yan Pi.

sentences.zh: 及太子廢，毗坐杖一百，與妻子俱配為官奴婢。

translations.literal: When the Crown Prince was deposed, Pi was sentenced to one hundred strokes of the cane and, together with his wife and children, was assigned as government slaves.
translations.idiomatic: When the Crown Prince was deposed, Yan Pi was sentenced to one hundred strokes of the cane and, together with his wife and children, was assigned as government slaves.

sentences.zh: 後二歲，放免為民。

translations.literal: Two years later, he was released and restored to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later, he was released and restored to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 煬帝嗣位，盛修軍器，以毗性巧，諳練舊事，詔典其職。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne, military equipment was greatly expanded; because Pi was ingenious by nature and well versed in old precedents, an edict put him in charge of that office.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne, military equipment was greatly expanded. Because Yan Pi was ingenious by nature and well versed in old precedents, an edict put him in charge of that office.

sentences.zh: 尋授朝請郎。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Attendant Consultant.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed Attendant Consultant.

sentences.zh: 毗立議，輦輅車輿，多所增損，語在《輿服志》。

translations.literal: Pi established proposals for imperial carriages and chariots, with many additions and reductions; the details are in the Treatise on Chariots and Robes.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Pi established proposals for imperial carriages and chariots, with many additions and reductions; the details are in the Treatise on Chariots and Robes.

sentences.zh: 擢拜起部郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted and appointed Attendant of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted and appointed Attendant of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗大備法駕，嫌屬車太多，顧謂毗曰：「開皇之日，屬車十有二乘，於事亦得。

translations.literal: The emperor once fully prepared the ritual escort and disliked that there were too many attendant chariots; turning to Pi he said: "In the Kaihuang era, there were twelve attendant chariots, which was also adequate for the purpose.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once fully prepared the ritual escort and disliked that there were too many attendant chariots. Turning to Yan Pi he said: "In the Kaihuang era, there were twelve attendant chariots, which was also adequate for the purpose.

sentences.zh: 今八十一乘，以牛駕車，不足以益文物。

translations.literal: Now there are eighty-one chariots, drawn by oxen — this is not enough to enhance ceremonial splendor.
translations.idiomatic: Now there are eighty-one chariots, drawn by oxen — this is not enough to enhance ceremonial splendor.

sentences.zh: 朕欲減之，從何為可？」

translations.literal: I wish to reduce them — from what number would it be acceptable?"
translations.idiomatic: I wish to reduce them — from what number would it be acceptable?"

sentences.zh: 毗對曰：「臣初定數，共宇文愷參詳故實，據漢胡伯始、蔡邕等議，屬車八十一乘，此起于秦，遂為後式。

translations.literal: Pi replied: "When your subject first fixed the number, together with Yu Wenkai he examined the ancient precedents; following the discussions of Hu Boshi, Cai Yong, and others of Han, attendant chariots numbered eighty-one — this began in Qin and became the later model.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Pi replied: "When I first fixed the number, together with Yu Wenkai I examined the ancient precedents. Following the discussions of Hu Boshi, Cai Yong, and others of Han, attendant chariots numbered eighty-one — this began in Qin and became the later model.

sentences.zh: 故張衡賦雲'屬車九九'是也。

translations.literal: Therefore Zhang Heng's rhapsody says 'attendant chariots nine times nine' — this is it.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore Zhang Heng's rhapsody says 'attendant chariots nine times nine' — this is it.

sentences.zh: 次及法駕，三分減一，為三十六乘。

translations.literal: Next for the ritual escort, one third was subtracted, making thirty-six chariots.
translations.idiomatic: Next for the ritual escort, one third was subtracted, making thirty-six chariots.

sentences.zh: 此漢制也。

translations.literal: This was the Han institution.
translations.idiomatic: This was the Han institution.

sentences.zh: 又據宋孝建時，有司奏議，晉遷江左，惟設五乘，尚書令、建平王宏曰：'八十一乘，議兼九國，三十六乘，無所准憑。

translations.literal: Also according to the Xiaojian era of Song, the relevant offices submitted a proposal: when Jin moved south of the Yangtze, only five chariots were set up; Director of the Masters of Writing, Prince of Jianping Hong, said: 'Eighty-one chariots, the proposal combining nine states; thirty-six chariots, with no basis to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Also according to the Xiaojian era of Song, the relevant offices submitted a proposal: when Jin moved south of the Yangtze, only five chariots were set up. Director of the Masters of Writing, Prince of Jianping Hong, said: 'Eighty-one chariots, the proposal combining nine states; thirty-six chariots, with no basis to follow.

sentences.zh: 江左五乘，儉不中禮。

translations.literal: The five chariots south of the Yangtze were too frugal and did not accord with ritual.
translations.idiomatic: The five chariots south of the Yangtze were too frugal and did not accord with ritual.

sentences.zh: 但帝王文物，旂旒之數，爰及冕玉，皆同十二。

translations.literal: But the ceremonial regalia of emperors and kings — the number of banners and tassels, extending to the crown and jade — are all twelve.
translations.idiomatic: But the ceremonial regalia of emperors and kings — the number of banners and tassels, extending to the crown and jade — are all twelve.

sentences.zh: 今宜准此，設十二乘。

translations.literal: Now it is fitting to follow this and set up twelve chariots.
translations.idiomatic: Now it is fitting to follow this and set up twelve chariots.

sentences.zh: '開皇平陳，因以為法。

translations.literal: When Kaihuang pacified Chen, this was adopted as the standard.
translations.idiomatic: When Kaihuang pacified Chen, this was adopted as the standard.

sentences.zh: 今憲章往古，大駕依秦，法駕依漢，小駕依宋，以為差等。」

translations.literal: Now taking the statutes of antiquity as model: the grand escort follows Qin, the ritual escort follows Han, the lesser escort follows Song — thus establishing the gradations."
translations.idiomatic: Now taking the statutes of antiquity as model: the grand escort follows Qin, the ritual escort follows Han, the lesser escort follows Song — thus establishing the gradations."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「何用秦法乎？

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Why use the Qin standard?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Why use the Qin standard?

sentences.zh: 大駕宜三十六，法駕宜用十二，小駕除之。」

translations.literal: The grand escort should be thirty-six, the ritual escort should use twelve, and the lesser escort should be abolished."
translations.idiomatic: The grand escort should be thirty-six, the ritual escort should use twelve, and the lesser escort should be abolished."

sentences.zh: 毗研精故事，皆此類也。

translations.literal: Pi's meticulous study of ancient precedents was all of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Pi's meticulous study of ancient precedents was all of this kind.

sentences.zh: 長城之役，毗總其事。

translations.literal: During the Great Wall project, Pi supervised the whole affair.
translations.idiomatic: During the Great Wall project, Yan Pi supervised the whole affair.

sentences.zh: 及帝有事恆嶽，詔毗營立壇場。

translations.literal: When the emperor performed rites at Mount Heng, an edict ordered Pi to build and establish the altar platform.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor performed rites at Mount Heng, an edict ordered Yan Pi to build and establish the altar platform.

sentences.zh: 尋轉殿內丞，從幸張掖郡。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Palace Attendant and accompanied the emperor on a visit to Zhangye Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to Palace Attendant and accompanied the emperor on a visit to Zhangye Commandery.

sentences.zh: 高昌王朝於行所，詔毗持節迎勞，遂將護入東都。

translations.literal: The King of Gaochang came to pay court at the traveling palace; an edict ordered Pi to hold the staff of office and welcome and comfort him, and thereupon escort him into the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Gaochang came to pay court at the traveling palace. An edict ordered Yan Pi to hold the staff of office and welcome him, and thereupon escort him into the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 尋以母憂去職。

translations.literal: Soon he left office due to mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he left office due to mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 未期，起令視事。

translations.literal: Before the mourning period ended, he was recalled and ordered to resume duties.
translations.idiomatic: Before the mourning period ended, he was recalled and ordered to resume duties.

sentences.zh: 將興遼東之役，自洛口開渠，達於涿郡，以通運漕。

translations.literal: When the Liaodong campaign was about to begin, a canal was opened from Luokou reaching to Zhuo Commandery to open transport and grain shipment.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liaodong campaign was about to begin, a canal was opened from Luokou reaching to Zhuo Commandery to open transport and grain shipment.

sentences.zh: 毗督其役。

translations.literal: Pi supervised the project.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Pi supervised the project.

sentences.zh: 明年，兼領右翊衛長史，營建臨朔宮。

translations.literal: The next year he additionally served as Chief Clerk of the Right Yiwu Guard and built Linshuo Palace.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he additionally served as Chief Clerk of the Right Yiwu Guard and built Linshuo Palace.

sentences.zh: 及征遼東，以本官領武賁郎將，典宿衛。

translations.literal: When the expedition to Liaodong was launched, in his original office he served as Colonel of the Martial Guard and managed night security.
translations.idiomatic: When the expedition to Liaodong was launched, in his original office he served as Colonel of the Martial Guard and managed night security.

sentences.zh: 時眾軍圍遼東城，帝令毗詣城下宣諭，賊弓弩亂髮，所乘馬中流矢，毗顏色不變，辭氣抑揚，卒事而去。

translations.literal: At that time the armies besieged Liaodong city; the emperor ordered Pi to go beneath the walls and proclaim the imperial message. The enemy's bows and crossbows fired wildly; the horse he rode was struck by an arrow, but Pi's expression did not change, his tone rose and fell with composure, and he finished the task and departed.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the armies besieged Liaodong city. The emperor ordered Yan Pi to go beneath the walls and proclaim the imperial message. The enemy's bows and crossbows fired wildly; the horse he rode was struck by an arrow, but Yan Pi's expression did not change, his tone rose and fell with composure, and he finished the task and departed.

sentences.zh: 尋拜朝請大夫，遷殿內少監，又領將作少監事。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Grand Attendant Consultant, promoted to Deputy Palace Attendant, and also took charge of the Deputy Chief of Palace Construction.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed Grand Attendant Consultant, promoted to Deputy Palace Attendant, and also took charge of the Deputy Chief of Palace Construction.

sentences.zh: 後複從帝征遼東，會楊玄感作逆，帝班師，兵部侍郎斛斯政奔遼東，帝令毗率騎二千追之，不及。

translations.literal: Later he again followed the emperor on the Liaodong expedition; it happened that Yang Xuangan rebelled, the emperor withdrew the army, and Vice Minister of War Husizheng fled to Liaodong. The emperor ordered Pi to lead two thousand cavalry in pursuit, but they did not catch him.
translations.idiomatic: Later he again followed the emperor on the Liaodong expedition. Yang Xuangan rebelled, the emperor withdrew the army, and Vice Minister of War Husizheng fled to Liaodong. The emperor ordered Yan Pi to lead two thousand cavalry in pursuit, but they did not catch him.

sentences.zh: 政據高麗柏崖城，毗攻之二日，有詔征還。

translations.literal: Zheng held Baicheng in Goguryeo; Pi attacked it for two days, then an edict ordered him recalled.
translations.idiomatic: Husizheng held Baicheng in Goguryeo. Yan Pi attacked it for two days, then an edict ordered him recalled.

sentences.zh: 從至高陽，暴卒，時年五十。

translations.literal: He followed the emperor to Gaoyang and died suddenly, at age fifty.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the emperor to Gaoyang and died suddenly, at age fifty.

sentences.zh: 帝甚悼惜之，贈殿內監。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply mourned and regretted it, and posthumously granted him the title of Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor deeply mourned his loss and posthumously granted him the title of Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 何稠 劉龍 黃亙 亙弟袞何稠，字桂林，國子祭酒妥之兄子也。

translations.literal: He Chou, Liu Long, Huang Gen — Gen's younger brother Gun. He Chou, courtesy name Guilin, was the nephew of the Director of the Imperial Academy, Tuo.
translations.idiomatic: He Chou, Liu Long, Huang Gen — Gen's younger brother Gun. He Chou, whose courtesy name was Guilin, was the nephew of the Director of the Imperial Academy, Tuo.

sentences.zh: 父通，善斫玉。

translations.literal: His father Tong was skilled at carving jade.
translations.idiomatic: His father Tong was skilled at carving jade.

sentences.zh: 稠性絕巧，有智思，用意精微。

translations.literal: Chou by nature was supremely ingenious, with intelligence and thought, applying his mind with exquisite precision.
translations.idiomatic: He Chou was supremely ingenious by nature, with intelligence and thought, applying his mind with exquisite precision.

sentences.zh: 年十餘歲，遇江陵陷，隨妥入長安。

translations.literal: At age ten and more, when Jiangling fell, he followed Tuo to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: At age ten and more, when Jiangling fell, he followed Tuo to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 仕周禦飾下士。

translations.literal: He served Zhou as a Lower Gentleman of Imperial Adornments.
translations.idiomatic: He served the Northern Zhou as a Lower Gentleman of Imperial Adornments.

sentences.zh: 及高祖為丞相，召補參軍，兼掌細作署。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen was Chancellor, he was summoned and appointed as Staff Officer, additionally managing the Fine Works Office.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen was Chancellor, He Chou was summoned and appointed as Staff Officer, additionally managing the Fine Works Office.

sentences.zh: 開皇初，授都督，累遷禦府監，曆太府丞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang he was granted the title Commander, was repeatedly promoted to Supervisor of the Imperial Storehouse, and served as Assistant Director of the Grand Storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Kaihuang he was granted the title Commander, was repeatedly promoted to Supervisor of the Imperial Storehouse, and served as Assistant Director of the Grand Storehouse.

sentences.zh: 稠博覽古圖，多識舊物。

translations.literal: Chou broadly read ancient diagrams and knew many old objects.
