translations.idiomatic: He Chou read widely in ancient diagrams and knew many old objects.

sentences.zh: 波斯嘗獻金綿錦袍，組織殊麗。

translations.literal: Persia once presented a brocade robe of gold thread, with a weave of extraordinary beauty.
translations.idiomatic: Persia once presented a brocade robe of gold thread, with a weave of extraordinary beauty.

sentences.zh: 上命稠為之。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Chou to make one.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered He Chou to make one.

sentences.zh: 稠錦既成，逾所獻者，上甚悅。

translations.literal: When Chou's brocade was completed, it surpassed the tribute piece, and the emperor was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: When He Chou's brocade was completed, it surpassed the tribute piece, and the emperor was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 時中國久絕琉璃之作，匠人無敢厝意，稠以綠瓷為之，與真不異。

translations.literal: At that time China had long lacked the making of glass; craftsmen dared not attempt it, but Chou made it from green porcelain, indistinguishable from the real thing.
translations.idiomatic: At that time China had long lacked the making of glass; craftsmen dared not attempt it, but He Chou made it from green porcelain, indistinguishable from the real thing.

sentences.zh: 尋加員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: Soon he was additionally appointed Attendant Cavalier.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was additionally appointed Attendant Cavalier.

sentences.zh: 開皇末，桂州俚李光仕聚眾為亂，詔稠召募討之。

translations.literal: At the end of Kaihuang, the Li chieftain Li Guangshi of Guizhou gathered a crowd and rebelled; an edict ordered Chou to recruit troops and suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Kaihuang, the Li chieftain Li Guangshi of Guizhou gathered a crowd and rebelled. An edict ordered He Chou to recruit troops and suppress him.

sentences.zh: 師次衡嶺，遣使者諭其渠帥洞主莫崇解兵降款。

translations.literal: The army halted at Heng Ridge and sent envoys to instruct the chieftain and cave lord Mo Chong to disband his troops and submit.
translations.idiomatic: The army halted at Heng Ridge and sent envoys to instruct the chieftain and cave lord Mo Chong to disband his troops and submit.

sentences.zh: 桂州長史王文同鎖崇以詣稠所。

translations.literal: Guizhou Chief Clerk Wang Wentong shackled Chong and brought him to Chou's camp.
translations.idiomatic: Guizhou Chief Clerk Wang Wentong shackled Chong and brought him to He Chou's camp.

sentences.zh: 稠詐宣言曰：「州縣不能綏養，致邊民擾叛，非崇之罪也。」

translations.literal: Chou falsely proclaimed: "The prefectures and counties could not pacify and nurture the people, causing frontier people to rebel — this is not Chong's fault."
translations.idiomatic: He Chou falsely proclaimed: "The prefectures and counties could not pacify and nurture the people, causing frontier people to rebel — this is not Chong's fault."

sentences.zh: 乃命釋之，引崇共坐，並從者四人，為設酒食而遣之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he ordered Chong released, invited him to sit together, along with four attendants, provided food and wine, and sent them away.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he ordered Chong released, invited him to sit together, along with four attendants, provided food and wine, and sent them away.

sentences.zh: 崇大悅，歸洞不設備。

translations.literal: Chong was greatly pleased, returned to his cave, and made no preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Chong was greatly pleased, returned to his cave, and made no preparations.

sentences.zh: 稠至五更，掩入其洞，悉發俚兵，以臨餘賊。

translations.literal: Chou at the fifth watch secretly entered the cave, mobilized all the Li troops, and advanced against the remaining rebels.
translations.idiomatic: He Chou at the fifth watch secretly entered the cave, mobilized all the Li troops, and advanced against the remaining rebels.

sentences.zh: 象州逆帥杜條遼、羅州逆帥龐靖等相繼降款。

translations.literal: The rebel leaders Du Tiaoliao of Xiangzhou and Pang Jing of Luozhou and others successively submitted.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel leaders Du Tiaoliao of Xiangzhou and Pang Jing of Luozhou and others successively submitted.

sentences.zh: 分遣建州開府梁昵討叛夷羅壽，羅州刺史馮暄討賊帥李大檀，並平之，傳首軍門。

translations.literal: He separately dispatched Jianzhou Area Commander Liang Ni to suppress the rebel Yi Luo Shou, and Luozhou Governor Feng Xuan to suppress the rebel leader Li Datan — both were pacified and their heads sent to the camp gate.
translations.idiomatic: He separately dispatched Jianzhou Area Commander Liang Ni to suppress the rebel Yi Luo Shou, and Luozhou Governor Feng Xuan to suppress the rebel leader Li Datan — both were pacified and their heads sent to the camp gate.

sentences.zh: 承制署首領為州縣官而還，眾皆悅服。

translations.literal: By imperial commission he appointed chieftains as prefectural and county officials and returned; all were pleased and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: By imperial commission he appointed chieftains as prefectural and county officials and returned; all were pleased and submitted.

sentences.zh: 有欽州刺史甯猛力，帥眾迎軍。

translations.literal: There was Qinzhou Governor Ning Mengli, who led his people to welcome the army.
translations.idiomatic: There was Qinzhou Governor Ning Mengli, who led his people to welcome the army.

sentences.zh: 初，猛力倔強山洞，欲圖為逆，至是惶懼，請身入朝。

translations.literal: At first Mengli had been stubborn in his mountain cave and wished to rebel; now he was fearful and requested to come to court in person.
translations.idiomatic: At first Mengli had been stubborn in his mountain cave and wished to rebel; now he was fearful and requested to come to court in person.

sentences.zh: 稠以其疾篤，因示無猜貳，遂放還州，與之約曰：「八九月間，可詣京師相見。」

translations.literal: Chou, because he was seriously ill, showed no suspicion and let him return to his province, making an appointment with him: "Between the eighth and ninth months, you may come to the capital to meet."
translations.idiomatic: He Chou, because Mengli was seriously ill, showed no suspicion and let him return to his province, making an appointment with him: "Between the eighth and ninth months, you may come to the capital to meet."

sentences.zh: 稠還奏狀，上意不懌。

translations.literal: Chou returned and submitted his report; the emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: He Chou returned and submitted his report; the emperor was displeased.

sentences.zh: 其年十月，猛力卒，上謂稠曰：「汝不前將猛力來，今竟死矣。」

translations.literal: That year in the tenth month Mengli died; the emperor said to Chou: "You did not bring Mengli here earlier — now he has died after all."
translations.idiomatic: That year in the tenth month Mengli died. The emperor said to He Chou: "You did not bring Mengli here earlier — now he has died after all."

sentences.zh: 稠曰：「猛力共臣為約，假令身死，當遣子入侍。

translations.literal: Chou said: "Mengli made an appointment with your subject; even if he died in person, he would send his son to attend court.
translations.idiomatic: He Chou said: "Mengli made an appointment with me; even if he died in person, he would send his son to attend court.

sentences.zh: 越人性直，其子必來。」

translations.literal: The Yue people are straightforward by nature — his son will surely come."
translations.idiomatic: The Yue people are straightforward by nature — his son will surely come."

sentences.zh: 初，猛力臨終，誡其子長真曰：「我與大使為約，不可失信于國士。

translations.literal: At first, when Mengli was near death, he admonished his son Changzhen: "I made an appointment with the envoy — you must not break faith with a man of the state.
translations.idiomatic: When Mengli was near death, he admonished his son Changzhen: "I made an appointment with the envoy — you must not break faith with a man of the state.

sentences.zh: 汝葬我訖，即宜上路。」

translations.literal: When you have buried me, you should set out on the road at once."
translations.idiomatic: When you have buried me, you should set out on the road at once."

sentences.zh: 長真如言入朝，上大悅曰：「何稠著信蠻夷，乃至於此。」

translations.literal: Changzhen came to court as instructed; the emperor was greatly pleased and said: "He Chou has established trust among the barbarians — even to this extent."
translations.idiomatic: Changzhen came to court as instructed. The emperor was greatly pleased and said: "He Chou has established trust among the frontier peoples — even to this extent."

sentences.zh: 以勳授開府。

translations.literal: For his merit he was granted the rank of Kaifu.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was granted the rank of Kaifu.

sentences.zh: 仁壽初，文獻皇后崩，與宇文愷參典山陵制度。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Renshou, when Empress Wenxian died, he together with Yu Wenkai jointly managed the institution of the imperial tomb.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Renshou, when Empress Wenxian died, he together with Yu Wenkai jointly managed the institution of the imperial tomb.

sentences.zh: 稠性少言，善候上旨，由是漸見親昵。

translations.literal: Chou by nature spoke little and was good at reading the emperor's intent; thereby he gradually came to be treated with intimacy.
translations.idiomatic: He Chou spoke little by nature and was good at reading the emperor's intent; thereby he gradually came to be treated with intimacy.

sentences.zh: 及上疾篤，謂稠曰：「汝既曾葬皇后，今我方死，宜好安置。

translations.literal: When the emperor's illness was grave, he said to Chou: "You have already buried the empress; now that I am about to die, you should arrange things well.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor's illness was grave, he said to He Chou: "You have already buried the empress; now that I am about to die, you should arrange things well.

sentences.zh: 屬此何益，但不能忘懷耳。

translations.literal: Entrusting this is of no benefit, but I cannot forget it.
translations.idiomatic: Entrusting this is of no benefit, but I cannot forget it.

sentences.zh: 魂其有知，當相見於地下。」

translations.literal: If my soul has awareness, we shall meet again in the underworld."
translations.idiomatic: If my soul has awareness, we shall meet again in the underworld."

sentences.zh: 上因攬太子頸謂曰：「何稠用心，我付以後事，動靜當共平章。」

translations.literal: The emperor then embraced the Crown Prince's neck and said: "He Chou's devoted service — I entrust the affairs after my death to him; in all actions you should consult with him jointly."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then embraced the Crown Prince's neck and said: "He Chou's devoted service — I entrust the affairs after my death to him; in all actions you should consult with him jointly."

sentences.zh: 大業初，煬帝將幸揚州，謂稠曰：「今天下大定，朕承洪業，服章文物，闕略猶多。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Daye, when Emperor Yang was about to visit Yangzhou, he said to Chou: "Now the realm is greatly settled, and I inherit the vast enterprise; robes, insignia, and ceremonial regalia still have many omissions.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Daye, when Emperor Yang was about to visit Yangzhou, he said to He Chou: "Now the realm is greatly settled, and I inherit the vast enterprise; robes, insignia, and ceremonial regalia still have many omissions.

sentences.zh: 卿可討閱圖籍，營造輿服羽儀，送至江都也。」

translations.literal: You should examine the diagrams and records, construct chariots, robes, and feathered banners, and send them to Jiangdu."
translations.idiomatic: You should examine the diagrams and records, construct chariots, robes, and feathered banners, and send them to Jiangdu."

sentences.zh: 其日，拜太府少卿。

translations.literal: That same day he was appointed Deputy Director of the Grand Storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he was appointed Deputy Director of the Grand Storehouse.

sentences.zh: 稠於是營黃麾三萬六千人仗，及車輿輦輅、皇后鹵簿、百官儀服，依期而就，送于江都。

translations.literal: Chou thereupon constructed thirty-six thousand yellow-banner guards and weapons, as well as chariots, imperial carriages, the empress's procession regalia, and the ceremonial robes of the hundred officials — all completed on schedule and sent to Jiangdu.
translations.idiomatic: He Chou thereupon constructed thirty-six thousand yellow-banner guards and weapons, as well as chariots, imperial carriages, the empress's procession regalia, and the ceremonial robes of the hundred officials — all completed on schedule and sent to Jiangdu.

sentences.zh: 所役工十萬餘人，用金銀錢物巨億計。

translations.literal: The laborers employed numbered more than one hundred thousand, and the gold, silver, and goods used amounted to hundreds of millions.
translations.idiomatic: The laborers employed numbered more than one hundred thousand, and the gold, silver, and goods used amounted to hundreds of millions.

sentences.zh: 帝使兵部侍郎明雅、選部郎薛邁等勾核之，數年方竟，毫釐無舛。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Vice Minister of War Ming Ya, Selection Bureau Director Xue Mai, and others to audit it; after several years it was finally completed, with not a fraction of error.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Vice Minister of War Ming Ya, Selection Bureau Director Xue Mai, and others to audit it. After several years it was finally completed, with not a fraction of error.

sentences.zh: 稠參會今古，多所改創。

translations.literal: Chou consulted past and present and made many innovations.
translations.idiomatic: He Chou consulted past and present and made many innovations.

sentences.zh: 魏、晉以來，皮弁有纓而無笄導。

translations.literal: Since Wei and Jin, the leather cap had tassels but no hairpin guide.
translations.idiomatic: Since Wei and Jin, the leather cap had tassels but no hairpin guide.

sentences.zh: 稠曰：「此古田獵之服也。

translations.literal: Chou said: "This is the garb of ancient hunting in the fields.
translations.idiomatic: He Chou said: "This is the garb of ancient hunting in the fields.

sentences.zh: 今服以入朝，宜變其制。」

translations.literal: Now to wear it at court, its institution should be changed."
translations.idiomatic: Now to wear it at court, its design should be changed."

sentences.zh: 故弁施象牙簪導，自稠始也。

translations.literal: Therefore the cap was fitted with an ivory hairpin guide — this began with Chou.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the cap was fitted with an ivory hairpin guide — this began with He Chou.

sentences.zh: 又從省之服，初無佩綬，稠曰：「此乃晦朔小朝之服。

translations.literal: Also the simplified court dress initially had no sash pendant; Chou said: "This is the garb for the minor audience at the new and full moon.
translations.idiomatic: Also the simplified court dress initially had no sash pendant. He Chou said: "This is the garb for the minor audience at the new and full moon.

sentences.zh: 安有人臣謁帝而去印綬，兼無佩玉之節乎？」

translations.literal: How can a minister attend the emperor and leave off the seal cord, and also lack the ornament of jade pendants?"
translations.idiomatic: How can a minister attend the emperor and leave off the seal cord, and also lack the ornament of jade pendants?"

sentences.zh: 乃加獸頭小綬及佩一隻。

translations.literal: Thereupon a small sash with beast-head ornament and one pendant were added.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon a small sash with beast-head ornament and one pendant were added.

sentences.zh: 舊制，五輅於轅上起箱，天子與參乘同在箱內。

translations.literal: Under the old institution, the five imperial chariots had boxes raised on the shafts; the Son of Heaven and the attendant rider sat together inside the box.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old institution, the five imperial chariots had boxes raised on the shafts; the Son of Heaven and the attendant rider sat together inside the box.

sentences.zh: 稠曰：「君臣同所，過為相逼。」

translations.literal: Chou said: "Ruler and minister in the same place — this is excessively cramped."
translations.idiomatic: He Chou said: "Ruler and minister in the same place — this is excessively cramped."

sentences.zh: 乃廣為盤輿，別構欄楯，侍臣立於其中。

translations.literal: Thereupon a broad platform carriage was made, with separate railings and shields constructed, and attending ministers stood within them.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon a broad platform carriage was made, with separate railings and shields constructed, and attending ministers stood within them.

sentences.zh: 于內複起須彌平坐，天子獨居其上。

translations.literal: Within, a Sumeru platform was additionally raised, and the Son of Heaven sat alone upon it.
translations.idiomatic: Within, a Sumeru platform was additionally raised, and the Son of Heaven sat alone upon it.

sentences.zh: 自餘麾幢文物，增損極多，事見《威儀志》。

translations.literal: As for the remaining banners, standards, and ceremonial regalia, additions and reductions were extremely numerous; the details are in the Treatise on Ceremonial Insignia.
translations.idiomatic: As for the remaining banners, standards, and ceremonial regalia, additions and reductions were extremely numerous; the details are in the Treatise on Ceremonial Insignia.

sentences.zh: 帝複令稠造戎車萬乘，鉤陳八百連，帝善之，以稠守太府卿。

translations.literal: The emperor again ordered Chou to make ten thousand war chariots and eight hundred linked Gouchen formations; the emperor approved, and Chou was appointed Director of the Grand Storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again ordered He Chou to make ten thousand war chariots and eight hundred linked Gouchen formations. The emperor approved, and He Chou was appointed Director of the Grand Storehouse.

sentences.zh: 後三歲，兼領少府監。

translations.literal: Three years later he additionally served as Supervisor of the Lesser Storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later he additionally served as Supervisor of the Lesser Storehouse.

sentences.zh: 遼東之役，攝右屯衛將軍，領禦營弩手三萬人。

translations.literal: During the Liaodong campaign, he served as acting General of the Right Tunwei Guard, commanding thirty thousand crossbowmen of the Imperial Camp.
translations.idiomatic: During the Liaodong campaign, he served as acting General of the Right Tunwei Guard, commanding thirty thousand crossbowmen of the Imperial Camp.

sentences.zh: 時工部尚書宇文愷造遼水橋不成，師不得濟，右屯衛大將軍麥鐵杖因而遇害。

translations.literal: At that time Minister of Works Yu Wenkai's construction of the Liao River bridge failed, the army could not cross, and Grand General of the Right Tunwei Guard Mai Tiezhang was killed as a result.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Minister of Works Yu Wenkai failed to build the Liao River bridge, the army could not cross, and Grand General of the Right Tunwei Guard Mai Tiezhang was killed as a result.

sentences.zh: 帝遣稠造橋，二日而就。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Chou to build the bridge; it was completed in two days.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent He Chou to build the bridge, and it was completed in two days.

sentences.zh: 初，稠制行殿及六合城，至是，帝于遼左與賊相對，夜中施之。

translations.literal: Earlier Chou had designed the mobile hall and the Six-Directions City; at this time the emperor faced the enemy on the Liao front, and it was deployed in the middle of the night.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier He Chou had designed the mobile hall and the Six-Directions City. Now, as the emperor faced the enemy on the Liao front, it was deployed in the middle of the night.

sentences.zh: 其城周回八裡，城及女垣合高十仞，上布甲士，立仗建旗。

translations.literal: The city was eight li in circumference; the wall and parapet together were ten ren high; armored soldiers were deployed on top, standing with weapons and raising banners.
translations.idiomatic: The city was eight li in circumference; the wall and parapet together stood ten ren high. Armored soldiers were deployed on top, standing with weapons and raising banners.

sentences.zh: 四隅置闕，面別一觀，觀下三門，遲明而畢。

translations.literal: At the four corners towers were placed; on each face a separate pavilion; beneath each pavilion three gates — it was completed by late dawn.
translations.idiomatic: Towers were placed at the four corners; on each face a separate pavilion; beneath each pavilion three gates — all completed by late dawn.

sentences.zh: 高麗望見，謂若神功。

translations.literal: Goguryeo saw it and said it was like divine power.
translations.idiomatic: The Goguryeo forces saw it and thought it the work of supernatural power.

sentences.zh: 是歲，加金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: That year he was additionally granted the title of Grand Master of Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was additionally granted the title of Grand Master of Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.

sentences.zh: 明年，攝左屯衛將軍，從至遼左。

translations.literal: The next year he served as acting General of the Left Tunwei Guard and followed the emperor to the Liao front.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he served as acting General of the Left Tunwei Guard and followed the emperor to the Liao front.

sentences.zh: 十二年，加右光祿大夫，從幸江都。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was additionally granted the title of Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and accompanied the emperor on a visit to Jiangdu.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he was additionally granted the title of Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and accompanied the emperor on a visit to Jiangdu.

sentences.zh: 遇宇文化及作亂，以為工部尚書。

translations.literal: When Yuwen Huaji rebelled, he was appointed Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuwen Huaji rebelled, He Chou was appointed Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 化及敗，陷於竇建德，建德複以為工部尚書、舒國公。

translations.literal: When Huaji was defeated, he fell into the hands of Dou Jiande, who again appointed him Minister of Works and Duke of Shu.
translations.idiomatic: When Huaji was defeated, He Chou fell into the hands of Dou Jiande, who again appointed him Minister of Works and Duke of Shu.

sentences.zh: 建德敗，歸於大唐，授將作少匠，卒。

translations.literal: When Jiande was defeated, he submitted to Great Tang and was appointed Deputy Chief of Palace Construction; he died.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiande was defeated, he submitted to Great Tang and was appointed Deputy Chief of Palace Construction, and there he died.

sentences.zh: 開皇時，有劉龍者，河間人也。

translations.literal: During Kaihuang there was a Liu Long, a native of Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: During Kaihuang there was a Liu Long, a native of Hejian.

sentences.zh: 性強明，有巧思。

translations.literal: By nature he was forceful and clear-minded, with ingenious ideas.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was forceful and clear-minded, with ingenious ideas.

sentences.zh: 齊後主知之，令修三爵台，甚稱旨，因而曆職通顯。

translations.literal: Emperor Houzhu of Qi knew of him and ordered him to repair the Three Goblets Terrace; it greatly pleased the emperor, and thereby he rose through offices to prominence.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Houzhu of Qi knew of him and ordered him to repair the Three Goblets Terrace. The work greatly pleased the emperor, and Liu Long rose through offices to prominence.

sentences.zh: 及高祖踐阼，大見親委，拜右衛將軍，兼將作大匠。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen ascended the throne, he was greatly trusted and appointed General of the Right Guard, additionally serving as Chief of Palace Construction.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen ascended the throne, Liu Long was greatly trusted and appointed General of the Right Guard, additionally serving as Chief of Palace Construction.

sentences.zh: 遷都之始，與高熲參掌制度，代號為能。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the capital relocation, together with Gao Jiong he jointly managed the institutions, and his generation called him capable.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the capital relocation, together with Gao Jiong he jointly managed the institutions, and his generation called him capable.

sentences.zh: 大業時，有黃亙者，不知何許人也，及其弟袞，俱巧思絕人。

translations.literal: During Daye there was a Huang Gen, of unknown origin, and his younger brother Gun — both had ingenuity surpassing other men.
translations.idiomatic: During Daye there was a Huang Gen, of unknown origin, and his younger brother Gun — both had ingenuity surpassing other men.

sentences.zh: 煬帝每令其兄弟直少府將作。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang often had the brothers serve on duty at the Lesser Storehouse and Palace Construction.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang often had the brothers serve on duty at the Lesser Storehouse and Palace Construction.

sentences.zh: 于時改創多務，亙、袞每參典其事。

translations.literal: At that time renovations and innovations were numerous; Gen and Gun each participated in managing these affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At that time renovations and innovations were numerous, and Gen and Gun each participated in managing these affairs.

sentences.zh: 凡有所為，何稠先令亙、袞立樣，當時工人皆稱其善，莫能有所損益。

translations.literal: In whatever was undertaken, He Chou first had Gen and Gun make models; the craftsmen of the time all praised them as good, and none could add or subtract anything.
translations.idiomatic: In whatever was undertaken, He Chou first had Gen and Gun make models. The craftsmen of the time all praised them as good, and none could add or subtract anything.

sentences.zh: 亙官至朝散大夫，袞官至散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: Gen reached the office of Grand Master of Palace Attendance; Gun reached the office of Attendant Cavalier.
translations.idiomatic: Gen reached the office of Grand Master of Palace Attendance; Gun reached the office of Attendant Cavalier.

sentences.zh: 【論】史臣曰：宇文愷學藝兼該，思理通贍，規矩之妙，參縱班、爾，當時制度，鹹取則焉。

translations.literal: [Commentary] The historian says: Yu Wenkai's learning and arts were comprehensive, his thought and reasoning thorough and ample; the subtlety of his standards rivaled Ban and Er — the institutions of his time all took him as their model.
translations.idiomatic: [Commentary] The historian says: Yu Wenkai's learning and arts were comprehensive, his thought and reasoning thorough and ample. The subtlety of his standards rivaled Ban and Er, and the institutions of his time all took him as their model.

sentences.zh: 其起仁壽宮，營建洛邑，要求時幸，窮侈極麗，使文皇失德，煬帝亡身，危亂之源，抑亦此之由。

translations.literal: His raising of Renshou Palace and construction of Luoyang, seeking the emperor's favor at every turn, exhausting extravagance to the utmost splendor — causing Emperor Wen to lose virtue and Emperor Yang to lose his life: the source of peril and chaos, perhaps, also lies in this.
translations.idiomatic: His raising of Renshou Palace and construction of Luoyang, seeking the emperor's favor at every turn and exhausting extravagance to the utmost splendor, caused Emperor Wen to lose virtue and Emperor Yang to lose his life. The source of peril and chaos, perhaps, also lies in this.

sentences.zh: 至於考覽書傳，定《明堂圖》，雖意過其通，有足觀者。

translations.literal: As for examining books and records and fixing the Bright Hall Diagram — although his intent exceeded his mastery, there is still much worth viewing.
translations.idiomatic: As for examining books and records and fixing the Bright Hall Diagram — although his intent exceeded his mastery, there is still much worth viewing.

sentences.zh: 毗、稠巧思過人，頗習舊事，稽前王之采章，成一代之文物。

translations.literal: Pi and Chou had ingenuity surpassing other men, were well versed in old precedents, examined the ceremonial regalia of former kings, and completed the cultural artifacts of an age.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Pi and He Chou had ingenuity surpassing other men, were well versed in old precedents, examined the ceremonial regalia of former kings, and completed the cultural artifacts of an age.

sentences.zh: 雖失之于華盛，亦有可傳於後焉。

translations.literal: Although they failed in excessive splendor, there is still much that can be passed down to posterity.
translations.idiomatic: Although they failed in excessive splendor, there is still much that can be passed down to posterity.
